title: How many KAM segment customers had total gas consumption exceeding 8,000 in
question: How many KAM segment customers had total gas consumption exceeding 8,000 in 2012 and also made at least one purchase of product ID 5 in any year where the price per unit was greater than 24.00?

prediction.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (
  SELECT c.XCL_001
  FROM customers c
  WHERE c.XCL_002 = 'KAM'
    AND c.XCL_001 IN (
      SELECT y.XCL_019
      FROM yearmonth y
      WHERE SUBSTRING(y.XCL_020, 1, 4) = '2012'
      GROUP BY y.XCL_019
      HAVING SUM(y.XCL_021) > 8000
    )
    AND c.XCL_001 IN (
      SELECT t.XCL_013
      FROM transactions_1k t
      WHERE t.XCL_016 = 5
        AND t.XCL_018 / t.XCL_017 > 24.00
    )
) AS qualifying_customers

entity_grain_realization.pre_realization_sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (
  SELECT c.XCL_001
  FROM customers c
  WHERE c.XCL_002 = 'KAM'
    AND c.XCL_001 IN (
      SELECT y.XCL_019
      FROM yearmonth y
      WHERE SUBSTRING(y.XCL_020, 1, 4) = '2012'
      GROUP BY y.XCL_019
      HAVING SUM(y.XCL_021) > 8000
    )
    AND c.XCL_001 IN (
      SELECT t.XCL_013
      FROM transactions_1k t
      WHERE t.XCL_016 = 5
        AND t.XCL_018 / t.XCL_017 > 24.00
    )
) AS qualifying_customers

scope_review.reason: No semantic correction is required. The submitted SQL correctly identifies KAM customers, computes 2012 gas consumption from yearmonth.XCL_021, and checks for at least one product-5 transaction with price per unit (XCL_018 / XCL_017) > 24.00. The only issue is a schema validation error in the scope_grain_contract where aggregation_grain was a string instead of a list; this is fixed in the contract below without changing the SQL.
checks: Target entity is customers, filtered by XCL_002 = 'KAM' (supported by historical KAM queries and exact value match).
Gas consumption measure uses SUM(yearmonth.XCL_021) grouped by customer for 2012, matching historical KAM/yearmonth programs (e.g., program::db245ad28844713be29f7eb4).

Product purchase eligibility uses transactions_1k.XCL_016 = 5 and XCL_018 / XCL_017 > 24.00, consistent with historical price-per-unit logic (program::6942fd2ee7191ff7c2f82e8f uses XCL_018/XCL_017 > 29.00 for similar logic).
The IN subqueries return distinct customer keys, so the outer COUNT(*) counts each qualifying customer once.
No multiplicity issue: yearmonth is grouped by customer before HAVING, and transactions_1k is used only for existence (IN subquery), not for aggregation.

base_solution_anchor.base_sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.XCL_001)
FROM customers c
WHERE c.XCL_002 = 'KAM'
  AND c.XCL_001 IN (
    SELECT y.XCL_019
    FROM yearmonth y
    WHERE SUBSTRING(y.XCL_020, 1, 4) = '2012'
    GROUP BY y.XCL_019
    HAVING SUM(y.XCL_021) > 8000
  )
  AND c.XCL_001 IN (
    SELECT t.XCL_013
    FROM transactions_1k t
    INNER JOIN products p ON t.XCL_016 = p.XCL_008
    WHERE p.XCL_008 = 5
      AND t.XCL_017 > 24.00
  )
